content:
Apple's MacBook Pro major revamp is coming soon, expected to debut in about a month at the earliest. This will be the first MacBook to feature a touchscreen, and also the first to adopt Tandem OLED. According to the latest issue of the 'Power On' newsletter, beyond these features, the new MacBook will be 'noticeably' lighter than the previous generation.

The newsletter reiterates that the new MacBook Pro should be announced 'before next month', meaning we should see these new machines before the end of November. This batch of new machines will come equipped with the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, as Apple has chosen to skip the high-end M6 series to accelerate the rollout of the M7.

The new MacBook Pro will be more lightweight

Although rumours about this batch of MacBooks have been circulating for some time, beyond the spec sheet details, we don't actually know much about them: OLED, touch, Dynamic Island, and so on. Past reports have described the computer as being thinner, but we've never had much of a visual concept. We still don't have one now, but there's an important new detail about how this machine will feel in hand:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman didn't specify exactly how much lighter it would be, but if you're currently using the existing MacBook Pro, especially the 16-inch model, you might find it slightly heavier than you'd like. Apple is reportedly working hard to improve this.

Beyond that, Gurman also mentioned that macOS Golden Gate will have some changes to support touch and Dynamic Island features, while macOS 27.2 will also officially debut.

Are you excited about the launch of this new batch of MacBook Pro? Would you buy one? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
